classification.difficultyReason: Identify the triangle as the smaller region, convert the area ratio into one third of the square and solve for its base using the square's height.

content.prompt: The straight line through the corner of the square below divides its area in the ratio of $1:2$. Find $x$.

spec.description: Square with top and left sides labelled 4. A segment connects the upper-left corner to an interior point on the bottom edge; the bottom-left segment is labelled x. Decorative uniform red fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Square side 4; the triangular region has perpendicular height 4 and base x.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown base remains labelled x; no answer is supplied.

answer.worked:
The triangle occupies the smaller region: its area is less than half the square's area.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=4^2\\A_{\text{square}}&=16\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac{1}{3}\times16\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac{16}{3}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{4x}{2}&=\frac{16}{3}\\2x&=\frac{16}{3}\\x&=\frac{8}{3}\end{align*}$$
